To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in COPD and BA, the development of ischemic arrhythmias is connected with structural and functional changes of RV and LV.
in COPD and BA the occurrence of suprventricular and ventricular extrasysytoles is connected with the development of myocardial ischemia.
in BA the occurrence of SV ES is connected with RV and LV diastic dysfunction and hypercholesterolia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of structural-functional changes in the myocardial condition on the development of myocardial ischemia in patients with COPD and BA.
the influence of structural changes and myocardial function on the development of myocardial ischemia in patients with COPD and BA.
the development of structural and functional myocardial changes in patients with BA and COPD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the occurrence of arrhythmia in patients with COPD and BA depends on myocardial structural and functional changes and myocardial ischemic condition.
the development of ischemic heart disease in patients with COPD and BA is connected with structural and functional changes of the myocardium, as well as with hypercholesterolemic dismetabolism.
the occurrence of arrhythmia depends on structural and functional myocardial changes, as well as on the presence of myocardial ischemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the myocardium is a target organ in COPD and BA, and the development of structural and functional abnormalities in the myocardium in these patients correlates with the occurrence of myocardial ischemia in COPD and with the development of arrhythmia in COPD as well as in BA.

myocardial ischemia depends on structural and functional alterations in RV and LV myocardium, while the appearance of extrasystoles is connected with the severity of the disease, and with the presence of RV and LV myocardial hypertrophy and dysfunction.

the development of arrhythmia in BA is connected with myocardial remodeling and the development of RV diastole dysfunction, as well in LV diastolic and systolic dysfunction, and in COPD with the development of LV systolic and diastolic dysfunction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the occurrence of SV and VES in patients with mild and moderate COPD depends on the condition of diastolic function of the right ventricle and the left ventricle and myocardial ischemic changes.
the development of myocardial ischemia in patients with COPD depends on the condition of LV and RV diastolic dysfunction.
the myocardial condition in BA and COPD is determined by the severity of the disease.
